title: Contributors
paragraphs: Abdullah Afzal is a researcher in theoretical physics at the School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Southampton. His research interests include quantum field theory and the foundations of physics.
Julian Barbour is an independent theoretical physicist. His research addresses the nature of time, quantum gravity, and the relational reformulation of dynamics.
Charles Alexandre Bédard is a researcher at École de technologie supérieure (ETS). His research interests include foundations of quantum mechanics, locality, and algorithmic information theory.
Giuseppe Di Pietra is a researcher at the University of Oxford. His research interests include quantum biology, non-classicality, and hybrid quantum-classical systems.

Aditya Iyer is a Visiting Researcher at the University of Oxford and CEO and co-founder of Allos AI. His research interests include quantum gravity signatures, quantum information theory, and cosmology.

Sam Kuypers is a researcher at Conjecture Institute. His research focuses on the foundations of quantum theory, with particular interests in the many-worlds theory, the nature of time, and the physics of time travel.
Chiara Marletto is a researcher at the Clarendon Laboratory, University of Oxford. Her research focuses on constructor theory, quantum information, and testing the quantum nature of gravity.
Simone Rijavec is a researcher at Tel Aviv University. His research focuses on the quantum nature of time.
Hassaan Saleem is a researcher in theoretical physics at the University at Albany. His research interests include string theory and supersymmetry.
Mia Stamatova is a researcher at the University of Oxford. Her research interests include quantum thermodynamics and spatiotemporal entanglement.

Vlatko Vedral is a researcher at the Clarendon Laboratory, University of Oxford. His research addresses quantum information theory, the foundations of quantum mechanics, and the relationship between information and physics.
Maria Violaris is a quantum physicist and science communicator. Her research interests include thermodynamics, quantum physics, and constructor theory.
David Wallace is a philosopher and physicist at the University of Pittsburgh. His interests include Many-Worlds quantum theory, probability in physics, and emergence.
Antonia Weber is a physicist at the University of Oxford. Her research interests include quantum gravity, testing the nature of gravity, and quantum cosmology.
